Subject: Question about Oct 31 invoice — unexpected token charge spike

Hope you had a good weekend. We were reviewing our October invoice and noticed a large, unexpected token spike on 2027-10-31 (line items attached). The total looks ~3.4x higher than our historical baseline for that day. Can you confirm whether this is expected or if there was a metering issue on your side?

We rely on predictable billing for budgeting, so any guidance here would be appreciated. If this is an error we’ll need a credit and a short explanation for our finance team.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erin Myers <erin@logicorp.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Root cause: cache-resync during autoscaling maintenance -> duplicate metering counts

Hannah / team / Erin —

Update from infra after an initial dig into the traces and metering: we had a cache-resync event at ~2027-10-31T03:12:00Z triggered by an autoscaler bounce in the serving pool. During the restart we replayed a small backfill of in-flight requests to rebuild the prefix cache. Two issues aligned and produced an overstated token tally for that maintenance window:

1) Replay duplication: the backfill replay logic retried several requests without deduplicating the metering key, so a subset of long-running chat sessions were counted twice.
2) Metering window rounding: the aggregation job that buckets tokens for the 1-hour windows overlapped the tail of the replay and included partial tokens twice due to an edge-case in our window boundary handling.

Scope: preliminary recount shows ~2.9x multiplier for sessions affected in the 03:12–03:40 UTC window for LogiCorp traffic. That maps to ~6.1k extra tokens billed on Oct 31 for this account (full recount attached).

Actions taken so far:
- Disabled the replay path and applied a hotfix to dedupe metering keys (deployed 02 Nov 02:00 UTC).
- Corrected aggregation window handling and kicked off a full recount job (INF-1723).
- Prepared a draft incident summary for customers.

Next steps for billing: Marissa, can you draft the provisional credit number once you compare the recount to the invoice? I’ll provide the log slices and a short evidence bundle (metering logs + request IDs) for audit.

Ben Carter
SRE Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: recount_spreadsheet_Logicorp.csv (csv)]

- Full refund for duplicated token units per the recount (see attached CSV).
- One-time goodwill credit for the operational disruption: $250.00.

Marissa Cole

Erin —

Thanks for signing — we’ve posted the $4,120.00 credit to your account just now. You should see the updated invoice attached to your account; I’ve also attached our one-paragraph summary below for your CFO.

One-paragraph summary for CFO:
On 2027-10-31, an autoscaler-triggered cache-resync caused a replay of in-flight requests that were not deduplicated by our metering path, and an aggregation window edge-case duplicated token counts for a subset of sessions. We calculated the overstated usage, applied a one-time credit of $4,120.00, and deployed a hotfix to deduplicate replayed requests and fix the aggregation boundary; the fix prevents recurrence. Full evidence (metering slices and logs) is available on request.

If you need a PDF version for ledger attaching, I can have Billing send one to billing@logicorp.com; please confirm.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll share the longer incident postmortem next week (INF-1723).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
